blocks.text: 0.1 grams of fat. Saturated fat is 0.01 grams, supporting a cleaner fat profile. Although the fat profile is almost irrelevant for fruits.

12.0 grams of carbs. Glycemic index is low at 45, meaning the carbs should land slower and steadier. Fibre is 3.6 grams, which gives a better fullness and digestion signal than most light fruits. Sugar is 4.3 grams, which is low for fruit and helps the carb section. Sugar control and fibre are the most important parts of the carbohydrate profile of fruits.
0.5 grams of protein. Not enough protein to be a real strength. For fruits, protein isn't really something to rely on.

Vitamin C is 16% daily value, useful for collagen formation and antioxidant support. Vitamin A is basically 0% daily value, not bringing much vision or immune support. For fruit, vitamin C and vitamin A matter most.

Potassium is 2% daily value, which is the best tracked mineral here, but still too low to matter much. Iron is only 1% daily value, not bringing much oxygen-transport support. For fruit, minerals are mostly just an extra bonus, and only matter when they are in amounts that actually mean something.

Pros first: sharp tart flavour tool. A small amount can brighten sauces, oats, salads, or baking without needing much fruit volume. Freezes well. It holds up well from frozen, so it is easier to keep around than many soft fresh fruits. Polyphenol-rich skin. The deep red skin brings a stronger plant-compound angle than many mild fruits.

Cons next: too tart for plain snacking. Most people do not eat raw cranberries by the handful, so the practical snack role is limited. Often needs added sugar. Cranberry sauces, juices, and dried versions commonly rely on sweetening to make the flavour work. Seasonal and recipe-dependent. Fresh cranberries are not as effortless year-round as everyday fruits like apples, bananas, or berries.
Best bits are low glycemic index and fibre. Weak spots are low minerals and vitamin A. Best for sharp low-calorie flavour swaps, and it makes a nice sauce. But that's about it.
